method: Hand-authored event log. Every event traces to a fact recorded in models.json (what_changed), data/v1/model-updates.md, or this wave's own pricing-table changes. Price events carry a before/after pair only where the record documents both numbers; otherwise the fields are null and the summary says why. The pricing baseline below is the pricing table as curated on 2026-10-11 — the drift engine diffs the live table against it, so a rate that moves from here on is caught mechanically, not by memory.

pricing_baseline.label: Pricing table as curated 2026-10-11 (Watchtower Wave A)

events.summary: Midjourney V1 Video launched: image-to-video only, 5s clips extendable to 21s, no native audio. Still the current Midjourney video model — no V2 announced as of Oct 2026.
Soul Cinema launched as a preview: one-click cinematic stills for image-to-video pipelines. Per-image pricing was not published at launch and still is not — the record stays verify-live.
PixVerse V6 launched with native audio in the same pass, 1–15s clips at up to 1080p, and 20+ prompt-driven camera controls. Sibling C1 followed on April 7 for action and VFX work.

Wan 2.7 launched (Tongyi Lab): Thinking Mode — the model plans the composition before generating — with the four-endpoint suite wan2.7-t2v, wan2.7-i2v, wan2.7-r2v, wan2.7-videoedit at 2–15s, 720p/1080p, and native audio. The last 2.x generation before Wan 3.0.
OpenAI closed the Sora apps and website. The API kept running for five more months — a staged shutdown, not a single date. New work should not have been planned on it from this day.
Grok Imagine Video 1.5 went GA with native audio in one pass. A July 31 update added 1080p, text-to-video, voice reference, and 7-reference scene control.
Kling 3.0 Turbo went GA with audio always on: $0.112/s at 720p, $0.14/s at 1080p on the API ladder.

MiniMax H3 (alias Hailuo 3.0) released as the new flagship: omni-modal context, 2K clips of 4–15s, native stereo audio. Hailuo 02 / 2.3 became the legacy generation the same day. Open weights were announced 'in the coming days' — no public repo confirmed as of Oct 11.
FLUX 3 Video reached the public (announced July 23): Black Forest Labs' first video model, up to 20s single takes at native 1080p with multilingual audio and lip-sync.
FLUX Video Upscale shipped: 1.5–3x upscaling to 4K for clips up to 20s.

Wan 3.0 formally released (public beta since August 6): native 30-second generations at 30fps — not stitched clips — with native audio. Alibaba Cloud Model Studio list: $0.05/s at 480p, $0.10/s at 720p, $0.20/s at 1080p. Third-party resync notes the same month report a ~38% cut on base 3.0 since launch; no absolute launch card was published, so the guide records the cut as reported, not as a rate.

gemini-omni-1.1-flash went GA: scene extension to 40s in 10s steps, first/last-frame interpolation, a 360p–4K ladder, and stateful multi-turn editing. In the Gemini app, Omni 1.1 Flash replaces Veo 3.1; the Veo API continues separately.
H3 Max gained native 1080p and a Turbo tier, per Krea's September 9 changelog. Single secondary source — the guide's H3 figures stay unchanged until a second confirmation lands.

Black Forest Labs listed QHD at $0.40/s and UHD at $0.80/s, with video-to-video at $0.65/s (QHD) and $0.95/s (UHD). These tiers were documented in the guide's model record but missing from its pricing table until Watchtower 2.0 added them.

Vidu S2 official details confirmed: S2-Avatar runs real-time at 720p (up from S1's 540p) with mid-session reference-image swaps and live-stream editing. A different product class from rendered clips — budget it differently.
Mirage Tesseract launched: an agent-driven editing and motion-graphics suite, not a generation model. The local engine is free; it lives in the guide's edit/post lane.

The Sora 2 API and /v1/videos shut down, completing the discontinuation that began with the April app closures. Routes return 410 — they do not come back. The record stays in the guide for the historical record only.

Kling 4.0 announced: Flash early access for Ultra Yearly subscribers, full release promised 'this October' — a month, not a date. No GA model ID, no API pricing, no independent benchmarks as of Oct 11. Status stays announced; do not plan shoots on it.
The gemini-omni-flash-preview endpoint was deprecated and now 404s with no fallback. Anything still calling the preview ID is broken; the GA 1.1 Flash ID is the live one.
Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite listed on Venice at a $0.04/clip entry point, ahead of the tier's full API rollout in early October.

Luma's legacy models (Ray 3, Ray 2, Ray 2 Flash, Ray 2 Relaxed, Ray 3 Reference, Ray 3 Refiner) hit their retirement deadline on the legacy API. Ray 3.2 on the Luma Agents API is the migration target; ComfyUI v0.39.0 deprecated its Ray 2 nodes in the same window.

BytePlus official rates re-read and confirmed — no change: $0.1028/s at 480p, $0.2311/s at 720p, $0.5686/s at 1080p. A confirmation is recorded as an event because budgets were built on these numbers; if they move, this is the baseline they move from.
Vidu Q4 Preview launched: cinematic 4K 10-bit, up to 15 image references, 16s maximum clips, image-to-video and reference-to-video only (no text-to-video).

The $0.014/s launch headline was a promotional off-peak floor, not a list rate. The official October 7 rate card lists $0.045/s at 540p, $0.12/s at 1080p, and $0.39/s at 4K, with image-to-video and reference-to-video at a 30% discount through November 30. The guide budgets from the list rates.

vivago R1 made available globally: a conversational production agent (script, storyboard, generation, edit in one run, up to 5-minute videos). Single-source launch coverage and no published rate card — verify live before planning around it.

Every record in the guide re-verified against October 2026 coverage. The automated check feed covered 22 models and flagged 0 changes and 0 errors. 'Veo 4' was re-verified as search bait for the third time: no announcement, no model card, no API ID exists.

PixVerse V6 added to the guide. A completeness audit found it was the most conspicuous uncovered model in the field: launched March 30, 2026, with an Artificial Analysis image-to-video Elo of 1,343 (April 2026) — and no record here. Now tracked like everything else.

PixVerse V6 pricing record added, closing the last gap in the pricing table (30 of 31 models covered became 31 of 31). Gateway-reported rates: about $0.09/s at 720p with audio, $0.18–0.23/s at 1080p. Third-party figures — verify live before budgeting.

FLUX 3's QHD, UHD, and video-to-video tiers added to the pricing table. They had been documented in the model record since the September 10 listing but never made it into the table the budget tools read — exactly the kind of silent gap the Watchtower diff now catches.

Automated source watch added: the Gemini API pricing page and the DeepMind Gemini model page. Omni had been tracked since its I/O 2026 unveiling with no watch at all; a token-billed rate now has a primary source to diff against.

Automated source watch added on Lightricks' official GitHub releases page. ltx.io refuses non-browser HTTP clients (connection dropped on repeated probes), so the releases page is the watchable official surface: fetched and recorded every run, excluded from the change signature because GitHub page chrome churns without a release.
Automated source watch added: Vidu's official pricing page and API platform. S2's per-clip rate was never officially published; the watch exists to catch the first rate card.

Automated source watch added: the official Tesseract product page at mirage.app. A free local engine has no rate card to diff; the watch tracks scope changes — export limits, account requirements, agent integrations.
Automated source watch added: Runway's official pricing page, where the Gen-4.5 credit rate and plan credit bundles are published.

Automated source watch added: Vidu's official pricing page and API platform, on top of the launch sources. The preview's promotional rates run through Nov 30; the watch is pointed at the rate card for the final pricing.
Automated source watch extended: BFL's official pricing page added alongside the bfl.ai homepage watch, giving the per-second tiers a primary source to diff against.
Automated source watch added: vivago's official pricing page. The record opened with no published rate; the watch is there to catch the first one.
Automated source watch added: the official PixVerse API docs and homepage. The guide's V6 rates are gateway-reported (third-party estimates); the docs are where a first-party rate card would land.

Automated source watch added: Higgsfield's help-center DoP guide. DoP had a full record and no sources at all — the last of the guide's models in that state alongside Marketing Studio. Tier and preset changes now have an official page to diff against.

Automated source watch added: Higgsfield's official API rate post and the platform pricing page. The record's per-clip credit costs are third-party; a republished rate table is now a review signal instead of a rumor.

Review pass on the Oct 12 checker flag: the moved source is a third-party startup directory listing, not a ByteDance page — no official announcement, model card, or pricing exists. Record stays reported/unconfirmed.
Review pass: the flagged klingai.com homepage moved on its Kling 4.0 hero banner — nothing about 3.0 changed. The homepage is signature-excluded from this run on; the record stands.
Review pass: the same klingai.com homepage move as Kling 3.0 — one rotating hero flagged every Kling model watching it. Homepage signature-excluded from this run on; the record stands.

Review pass: the moved source is an ABNewswire press-release review of the Hailuo Video Agent — third-party wire copy that no longer answers the checker at all. No MiniMax source moved; the record stands.
Review pass: the moved source is a competitor's comparison post (Magic Hour); its Luma figures match the plans already on record. No Luma source moved; the record stands.
Review pass: the moved source is Magic Hour's Pika pricing roundup — $10 Starter, $35 Creator, the plans already on record. The record stands.
Review pass: the moved source is a CometAPI aggregator post that moved twice in an hour on site chrome alone; it joins the signature-exclusion list. No Midjourney source moved; the record stands.

Review pass: the flagged sources are the klingai.com 4.0 hero and IPO coverage of the Sept 28 unveil. Still no GA model ID in the official API docs and no published pricing — the standing watch's own criteria for flipping this record. Record stays announced, Flash early access only.

Watchtower calibration: the re-baseline run flagged 17 models, and the flags traced to signature-unstable pages — GitHub blob pages embed per-request nonces (two consecutive fetches, two signatures) and now sit outside the change signature globally, and 26 blog/listing/homepage URLs with rotating rails were excluded per-model. Every source is still fetched and recorded each run; no model record changed.

Review pass: the flagged source is a third-party blog post (lapaasvoice.com) whose page is signature-stable across repeat fetches and identical to the flagged run — the move was against the older baseline. Its claims (S2-Avatar, S2-Editing, 720p real-time) match the record, it publishes no rate, and Vidu's official pricing page signature is unchanged. No record change.

Standing watch re-checked: APIMart still lists the Kling 4.0 API as a preview ('Not yet... prices and billing rules will be published when access is confirmed') and the klingai.com hero is unchanged. Still no GA model ID in the official API docs and no published pricing — the watch's own criteria. Record stays announced, Flash early access only.

First published Soul Cinema rate: Higgsfield's own API post lists a $0.0032/image starting rate, now tabled in pricing.json. The in-app per-image credit cost is still unpublished, so the standing watch narrows to that figure.

Standing watch resolved: the open-weights drop it was set for (Aug 3, 2026, base checkpoint) is already on record, and the record now also carries the license term the watch asked for — the MiniMax H3 Community License excludes local deployment in the US, EU, UK, and South Korea; the hosted API is unaffected. The watch is retired.

Standing watch verified: Wan 2.7 clears the criteria the desk applies — official Alibaba Cloud model IDs (wan2.7-t2v, wan2.7-i2v, wan2.7-r2v, wan2.7-videoedit) and published list pricing (¥0.6/s at 720p, ¥1.0/s at 1080p; hosted on fal at $0.10/s and $0.15/s), confirmed across independent sources. It is not in models.json yet: adding a model goes through the research-artifact chain as its own records change, not a review-pass edit. The watch stays open until the record lands.

Wan 2.7 added to the guide through the research-artifact chain (Watchtower 2.4). The gap was flagged in wave 21 and verified in Watchtower 2.3 — official Alibaba Cloud model IDs and published list pricing both exist — but a review pass does not hand-add models; this records change is the addition the watch asked for. The standing watch is resolved and retired.

Wan 2.7 pricing record added (coverage 31 of 31 becomes 32 of 32). Alibaba Cloud Model Studio list: $0.10/s at 720p and $0.15/s at 1080p on every wan2.7 video endpoint, corroborated by fal hosting the same card at the same rates; China list ¥0.6/s / ¥1.0/s. The first Wan record priced from a published USD list rather than Higgsfield credits.

Automated source watch added: the model's own sources (the PoYo model page carrying the official endpoint IDs and fal's rates, CreateVision's spec registry) plus the official Wan site at wan.video. A published USD list card is exactly the kind of surface whose move matters — the watch diffs it from the first run.

Standing watch re-checked (Watchtower 2.4): no official ByteDance announcement exists — ByteDance's catalog still tops out at Seedance 2.5, and current coverage is third-party explainers and an unofficial tracking site saying the same. Record stays reported/unconfirmed; the watch stays open.

Standing watch re-checked (Watchtower 2.4): the full model is still staged for October with no date — Flash early access (Ultra Yearly, 3–20s at 720p) is the only live tier, API packs still do not cover 4.0, and there is still no GA model ID and no published pricing. The criteria are unchanged and unmet; the record stays announced.

Standing watch re-checked (Watchtower 2.4): the in-app per-image credit cost is still not published by Higgsfield — the only figures in circulation remain third-party (~0.125 credits/image, the figure already on record as third-party). The published rate on record stays the API starting rate ($0.0032/image, Watchtower 2.3); the narrowed watch stays open.

Review pass: the checker flagged Higgsfield's API post — the page carrying Soul Cinema's $0.0032/image rate — but two consecutive fetches return two different signatures at identical length (the page embeds a rotating prompt-library payload), and its rate table still lists $0.0032/image, the figure on record. The URL is signature-excluded for this model from this run on (still fetched and recorded); no record change.

Standing watch re-checked (Watchtower 2.5): no official ByteDance announcement exists — the daily-checked release tracker confirms ByteDance's catalog still lists Seedance 2.5 as current, and the status audit notes no Seedance 3 product, model card, API identifier, price, or release schedule in the official directory. Record stays reported/unconfirmed; the watch stays open.

Standing watch re-checked (Watchtower 2.5): APIMart's Kling 4.0 page is signature-identical to the Watchtower 2.4 baseline and still reads 'API Coming Soon' with pricing 'not been announced'; independent reviews confirm no model identifier and no price for either tier. Third-party subscription listings (kling4.tv) are not official pricing and carry no GA model ID. Record stays announced, Flash early access only; the watch stays open.

Standing watch re-checked (Watchtower 2.5): the in-app per-image credit cost is still not published by Higgsfield — its pricing page carries no Soul Cinema credit figure, and the API post's rate table still lists only the $0.0032/image API starting rate tabled in Watchtower 2.3. The only credit figures in circulation remain third-party (~0.125 credits/image). The narrowed watch stays open.

Post-addition stability confirmed (Watchtower 2.5), one pass after Wan 2.7 joined through the artifact chain: the PoYo model page and CreateVision's spec registry returned signatures identical to the Watchtower 2.4 baseline, and the final feed carries the model stable/ok — its watch severity is only its own baseline pricing diff, the PixVerse pattern holding. The one flag touching the model this pass was the shared upgrademag launch report, adjudicated as intermittent variant churn and signature-excluded for both Wan models.

Review pass: the flagged source is a third-party multi-model pricing roundup whose living LLM token tables moved; it carries no Veo per-second rate contradicting the record, and the page is signature-identical across repeat fetches and to the flagged run. No Google source moved; the record stands.

Review pass: the flagged source is the shared upgrademag Wan 2.7 launch report — it flagged in two consecutive runs on intermittent variant fetches (rotating headlines rail) while the settled page matches across repeated fetches and its launch facts are the record's own. The URL is signature-excluded for both Wan models from this pass (still fetched and recorded every run); no record change.

Review pass: BFL's official pricing page was redesigned from a static rate table (22,122 chars) to a JS calculator shell (2,249 chars) whose fetched text carries no per-second video rate — nothing on it contradicts the record's FLUX 3 rates, which stand as documented from the September 10 listing. The URL stays signature-live by design: it is the primary rate source, and a readable rate move should flag.

Standing watch re-checked (Watchtower 2.6): still no official ByteDance announcement — the release tracker's daily inspection still rests on its Oct 6 catalog check listing Seedance 2.5 as current, and current coverage agrees no announcement, API, or date exists. The record's standing position (reported, unconfirmed) is unchanged and the watch stays open.

Standing watch re-checked (Watchtower 2.6): APIMart's criteria page returned a signature identical to the 2.4/2.5 baseline and still reads 'API Coming Soon' with pricing not announced; current coverage still describes Flash-only subscriber access and no published API pricing. No GA model ID and no published pricing from Kuaishou — the record stays 'announced' and the watch stays open.

Standing watch re-checked (Watchtower 2.6): the in-app per-image credit cost is still not published by Higgsfield — its pricing page is a 428-char app shell with no credit figure, and the API post's rate table still lists only the $0.0032/image API starting rate tabled in Watchtower 2.3. The only credit figures in circulation remain third-party (~0.125 credits/image). The narrowed watch stays open.

Readable primary rate source added (Watchtower 2.6): bfl.ai/pricing is now a JS calculator shell a static fetch cannot read rates from, so BFL's official docs pricing page (docs.bfl.ai/quick_start/pricing) joins the watch as a signature-live source. Probed with the checker's fetch path first — its FLUX 3 Video table matches the record exactly ($0.06 draft / $0.17 hd / $0.29 fhd / $0.40 qhd / $0.80 uhd for text/image-to-video; $0.12 draft / $0.41 / $0.53 / $0.65 / $0.95 for video continuation), so no rate changed. bfl.ai/pricing stays signature-live alongside it.

Review pass: the flagged source is Higgsfield's pricing page, a 428-char app shell whose text is a navigation list with no plan, credit, or rate figure on it. Its signature moved once on nav chrome and then held across three fresh fetches and the re-baseline run; nothing on it contradicts the record, whose per-clip credit costs remain third-party as documented. The URL stays signature-live and the record stands.
